subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw design a gateway-side credential forwarding flow?
rationale: The remaining fix crosses the provider credential and node/gateway trust boundary, and current closed PRs proposed both fail-closed and forwarding shapes without a merged maintainer decision.

options.title: Fail closed before auth
options.body: Block login when node-host config points at a non-loopback gateway and instruct the user to run auth on the gateway host.

options.title: Design gateway forwarding
options.body: Add an authenticated gateway-side credential flow that stores OAuth material directly in the gateway agent auth store.

options.title: Warn and allow
options.body: Keep node-local writes possible after a warning, accepting the risk that users can still consume refresh tokens into the wrong store.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth
recommendation.body: Block login when node-host config points at a non-loopback gateway and instruct the user to run auth on the gateway host.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the closed maintainer draft for the narrow fail-closed fix and have recent auth-profile ownership signals.
